description: rnews.rs:56-58 — The comment says .take(limit+1) enforces the cap 'without allocating the full oversized output first' and 'without allocating beyond limit+1'. This is misleading. read_to_end() DOES buffer all bytes read into 'out' (up to limit+1 bytes), so it WILL allocate up to ~50 MiB on the heap for a near-limit batch. What .take() actually prevents is reading MORE than limit+1 bytes from the GzDecoder — it stops the streaming decode early. The allocation of limit+1 bytes is not avoided. Fix: rewrite the comment to say what .take() actually does: 'stops the streaming decoder after limit+1 bytes, so the decompressor never reads beyond that point; the output buffer still grows to at most limit+1 bytes.'
title: decompress_gunbatch: misleading comment about allocation
